codeReview.summary: Solid implementation that correctly wires up Factory quota display into the CLI. All seven feature requirements are addressed: handleFactory dispatcher with quota/help subcommands, handleFactoryQuota with full account loading + usage fetching + box rendering, handleQuota modified to include Factory for scope='all'/'factory', 'factory' namespace routing in main(), printHelp() updated, graceful degradation for no-accounts, and proper barrel re-exports. The code follows existing Codex/Claude patterns closely. 22 new tests cover routing, display, JSON output, label filtering, billing-day, no-accounts errors, and API key masking. Security is handled correctly — no sensitive tokens/keys appear in display or JSON output.

issues.description: FACTORY_AUTH_KEY_PATH is imported from constants.js but never used in the handlers module. It's included in the import block alongside FACTORY_MULTI_ACCOUNT_PATH and FACTORY_AUTH_FILE_PATH, but only the latter two are referenced in the 'no accounts' error output. The key file is a companion to the auth file so omitting it from user-facing messages is reasonable, but the unused import should be cleaned up.

Duplicate computation of billing-day index. The variable billingDayIdx (line 52) and billingDayArgIdx (line 76) both compute args.indexOf('--billing-day'). The second lookup exists solely to populate the flagsWithValues set for nonFlagArgs filtering. Could consolidate to reuse a single const, but this is a minor DRY concern with no functional impact.

handleFactory's default case for unknown subcommands prints an explicit error message ('Unknown Factory command: X') before showing help, while handleCodex and handleClaude's default cases silently show help and exit. This is actually better UX for handleFactory but creates a minor inconsistency across namespace dispatchers. Consider aligning all three in a future pass.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The --billing-day flag introduces a new pattern: flags with values (--flag N). The main() arg parser now has special handling to exclude the flag's value from nonFlagArgs. If future flags with values are added (e.g., --output-format, --timeout), this manual exclusion approach will become unwieldy. AGENTS.md and architecture docs don't document this flag-value parsing pattern or suggest a general approach.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: shuvquota.js lines 52-60 (billingDayIdx parsing) and lines 74-80 (flagsWithValues set). Each new flag-with-value would need its own indexOf + Set.add pair.

sharedStateObservations.observation: handleQuota was not previously exported as a barrel re-export in shuvquota.js. This commit adds it, enabling direct test invocation. The AGENTS.md architecture section doesn't note that handleQuota is the central quota aggregator that combines all providers, which may be useful for future workers extending it.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: shuvquota.js barrel re-exports block — handleQuota added at line 291 alongside handleFactory/handleFactoryQuota.

summary: The Factory quota handlers implementation passes review. All seven feature requirements are fully implemented: Factory namespace routing, handleFactory dispatcher, handleFactoryQuota with account loading/usage fetching/box rendering, handleQuota Factory integration, updated help text, graceful degradation, and barrel re-exports. The code closely follows existing Codex/Claude patterns. 22 well-structured tests cover routing, display, JSON output, label filtering, billing-day, no-accounts errors, and API key masking (VAL-SEC-001). Three non-blocking issues found: an unused FACTORY_AUTH_KEY_PATH import, duplicate billing-day index computation, and a minor pattern inconsistency in unknown-subcommand error handling. Two shared-state observations noted about the flag-with-value parsing pattern and the newly-exported handleQuota function.
